SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/r2.claim: Al-Sajda places livestock before people after mentioning crops, while Abasa puts people first because its context first discusses human food and then livestock fodder.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه لما تقدم ذكر الزرع في آية السجدة ناسب تقديم الأنعام، بخلاف آية عبس فإنها في طعام الإنسان

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r6.claim: Quraysh mock the promised dominance and ask when it will arrive, but accepting it at that time will be useless; the Prophet should leave them to wait.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r6.anchor: professing faith in it will be of no avail to these people who are making fun of it today.

STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r1.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r16.claim: The discussion calls readers to reflect on past civilizations and God's signs in creation.
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r16.anchor: A call to reflect upon the end of civilizations past and the signs of God in creation (vv. 26–27)

SAMIN-DURR:32:27/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:27/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
SAMIN-DURR:32:27/r1.claim: The common reading uses third-person; Ibn Masud reads second-person as iltifat.
SAMIN-DURR:32:27/r1.anchor: قوله: { يبصرون }: العامة على الغيبة، وابن مسعود على الخطاب التفاتا.

SAMIN-DURR:32:27/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:27/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:32:27/r2.claim: A variant has الجرز with silent راء; its discussion was given at the beginning of al-Kahf.
SAMIN-DURR:32:27/r2.anchor: وقرئ " الجرز " بسكون الراء. وقد تقدم أول الكهف.

ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r9.claim: The passage reports several vocalized forms of الجرز; the excerpt gives the same undiacritized spelling for them.

ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r10.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r10.claim: A tafsīr report identifies the barren land as Yemen.
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r10.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنها أرض اليمن، والجرز عند أهل اللغة

ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r11.claim: In the language, الجرز is land that grows nothing; the explanation links it to land that consumes its vegetation.
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r11.anchor: والجرز عند أهل اللغة الأرض التي لا تنبت.

ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r12.claim: The related forms جزوز and جراز describe, respectively, a voracious woman and a sword that cuts things off completely.
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r12.anchor: يقال امرأة جزوز إذا كانت أكولا، ويقال: سيف جراز

ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r13.claim: The form جرز with a still rāʾ is a lightened form of جرز.
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r13.anchor: فمن قال جرز فهو تخفيف جرز

ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r14.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r14.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r14.claim: The other two forms are dialect variants.
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r14.anchor: ومن قال: جرز وجرز فهما لغتان.

ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r15.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r15.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r15.claim: جرز may be a verbal noun used adjectivally: the land is described as possessing plant-consuming activity.
ZAJJAJ:v4p210/r15.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جرز مصدرا وصف به كأنه أرض ذات جرز

ASAD-NOTES:32:27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:32:27/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:32:27/r1.claim: Asad makes the revival of barren land and its crops a sign pointing to resurrection.
ASAD-NOTES:32:27/r1.anchor: Can they not, then, see [the truth of resurrection]?

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p41/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p41/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p41/r1.claim: Al-Sajda mentions livestock before people because the preceding subject is crops, which suits the livestock being named first.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p41/r1.anchor: فقدم الأنعام على الناس. وقال في مكان آخر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p492/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p492/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p492/r1.claim: In 32:27 livestock precede people because the preceding mention is crops, which are presented as livestock feed first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p492/r1.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر الزرع في آية السجدة ناسب تقديم الأنعام

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#4/r1.claim: Mujahid describes the barren land as land that does not grow anything.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ أفلا يسمعون أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز ﴾ قال هي أبين التي لا تنبت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r1.claim: After arguing from earlier nations destroyed for disbelief, God argues from displaying His power and alerting people to resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r1.anchor: فأهلكوا، ثم أقامها عليهم بإظهار قدرته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r2.claim: As explained at 18:8, “al-jarz” is any barren land, not one specific place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r2.anchor: وتقدم تفسير الجرز في الكهف، وكل أرض جزر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies it as Abyan in Yemen, watered by runoff rather than rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هي أرض أبين من اليمن، وهي أرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r4.claim: A variant reads the rāʾ as quiescent.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r6.claim: Crops are singled out though water produces useful plants because crops are honored and most important; “crop” stands for vegetation generally.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r6.anchor: وخص الزرع بالذكر، وإن كان يخرج الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r7.claim: Livestock come first because they eat growth as soon as it appears, before people eat grain and fodder is harvested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r7.anchor: وقدمت الأنعام، لأن ما ينبت يأكله الأنعام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r8.claim: Other reasons are that animals eat fodder while people have other foods, or that the verse moves from lower creatures to noble humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r8.anchor: أو لأنه غذاء الدواب، والإنسان قد يتغذى بغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r9.speaker: أبو حيوة، أبو بكر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة، وأبو بكر في رواية: يأكل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r10.claim: The majority read “yubṣirūn” in the third person.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the closing question as direct address.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r12.claim: The close suits a visible sign; the preceding verse concerns what is heard and asks whether they hear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p441/r12.anchor: وجاءت الفاصلة: أفلا يبصرون، لأن ما سبق مرئي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r1.claim: As with the preceding verse's awalam yahdi, the rhetorical question asks whether they are blind and have not witnessed the sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r1.anchor: الكلام فيه كالكلام في ( أو لم يهد ) أي أعموا ولم يشاهدوا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r2.claim: God drives the water by driving clouds that carry it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r2.anchor: إنا نسوق الماء ( بسوق السحاب الحامل له

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r3.claim: Another explanation is that God drives the water itself by means of floods.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r4.claim: A further explanation is that God conducts water through rivers and springs.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : بإجرائه في الأنهار ومن العيون

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r5.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r5.claim: Al-Kashshāf glosses the barren land as land whose vegetation has been cut away, either for want of water or because grazing and removal cleared it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r5.anchor: أي التي جرز نباتها أي قطع إما لعدم الماء وإما لأنه رعى وأزيل كما في الكشاف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r6.speaker: مجمع البيان
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r6.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān calls it dry, plantless land after rain stops; the root evokes cutting, as with a cutting sword, an all-consuming camel, or a greedy man, illustrated by a rajaz line.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r6.anchor: في مجمع البيان الأرض الجرز اليابسة التي ليس فيها نبات

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r7.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib defines jarz as vegetation cut from its root and land eaten bare, cites a proverb about total consumption, and connects severe coughing with the sense of cutting.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r7.anchor: الراغب : الجرز منقطع النبات من أصله وأرض مجروزة أكل ما عليها وفي مثل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r8.claim: Al-Rāghib's sense of jarz as naturally non-growing salt-flat land does not fit this context, since the verse says crops are brought forth there.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r8.anchor: وهو غير مناسب هنا لقوله تعالى : ( فنخرج به زرعا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r9.claim: The apparent meaning is any land that has become characterized by barrenness, without restricting it to a named place.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r9.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد الأرض المتصفة بهذه الصفة أي أرض كانت

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the barren land as villages between Yemen and Syria.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r10.anchor: وأخرج إبن أبي حاتم عن الحسن أنها قرى بين اليمن والشام

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies it as land in Yemen, in reports transmitted by several collectors.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r11.anchor: وأخرج هو وإبن جرير وإبن المنذر وإبن أبي شيبة عن إبن عباس أنها أرض باليمن

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r12.claim: Mujāhid calls it non-growing land, such as the plain and similar terrain, without limiting the expression to a particular named territory.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r12.anchor: ذهب مجاهد أخرج عنه جماعة أنه قال : الأرض الجرز هي التي لا تنبت

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r13.speaker: قرئ
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r13.claim: A variant reads al-jarz with a silent rāʾ.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r14.claim: The pronoun in by it refers to the water.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r14.anchor: وضمير ( به ) للماء والكلام على ظاهره عند السلف الصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r15.speaker: السلف الصالح
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r15.claim: The early pious authorities take the wording at its apparent, literal sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r15.anchor: والكلام على ظاهره عند السلف الصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r16.speaker: الأشاعرة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r16.claim: The Ashʿarites understand it as God bringing forth the crop at the water's arrival, rather than water directly producing it.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r17.claim: Zarʿ is originally a verbal noun used for what is planted; here it means all growth produced by rain, including trees, so livestock eat straw, fodder, leaves, and some grain, while people eat legumes and grains.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r17.anchor: والزرع في الأصل مصدر وعبر به عن المزروع والمراد به ما يخرج بالمطر مطلقا فيشمل الشجر وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r18.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r18.claim: Al-Baḥr allows zarʿ to mean either familiar cultivated crops, singled out for honor and because they are the main purpose, or vegetation in general.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r18.anchor: وفي البحر يجوز أن يراد بالزرع النبات المعروف وخص بالذكر تشريفا له ولأنه أعظم ما يقصد من النبات

ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r19.claim: Livestock are mentioned before people because their food is limited to this growth and they eat it before it fruits and grains; another view says the order rises from lower to higher, the children of Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p139#2/r19.anchor: وقدم الأنعام لأن انتفاعها مقصور على ذلك والإنسان قد يتغذى بغيره ولأن أكلها منه مقدم لأنها تأكله قبل أن يثمر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r1.speaker: أبو حيوة وأبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r1.claim: Abū Ḥaywa and Abū Bakr in one transmission read yaʾkul with yāʾ rather than taʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وأبو بكر في رواية ( يأكل ) بالياء التحيتة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r2.claim: The question urges them to see this sign and infer God's perfect power and bounty.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r2.anchor: أي ألا يبصرون فلا يبصرون ذلك ليستدلوا به على كمال قدرته تعالى وفضله عزوجل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r3.claim: The ending says they see because what precedes is visible; the preceding verse instead ends with hearing because it concerns what is heard.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r3.anchor: وجعات الفاصلة هنا ( يبصرون ) لأن ما قبله مرئي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r4.claim: Another explanation sees a progression to a higher admonition, intensifying the reminder and removing any excuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r4.anchor: وقيل : ترقيا إلى الأعلى في الإتعاظ مبالغة في التذكير

ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads tabṣirūn with second-person tāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p140/r5.anchor: وقرأ إبن مسعود ( تبصرون ) بالتاء الفوقية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r9.claim: The barren land is dry, rough, and without vegetation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r9.anchor: أي: اليابسة الغليظة التي لا نبات فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies it as land in Yemen.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي أرض باليمن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r11.claim: Mujahid identifies it as land in Babel.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p309#2/r12.claim: Animals eat grass and straw from the crop, while people eat its grains and staple foods.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r6.claim: The land is one whose vegetation has been cut away, not land that never grows, since God brings crops from it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r6.anchor: التي جرز نباتها أي قطع وأزيل لا التي لا تنبت

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r7.claim: Another view takes al-jarz as a place in Yemen.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r8.claim: Vegetation feeds livestock, such as figs and foliage, while people eat grain and fruit.
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r8.anchor: من الزرع. { أنعمهم } كالتين والورق. { وأنفسهم } كالحب والثمر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r9.claim: Crops should make people recognize God’s complete power and bounty.
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:25-27/r9.anchor: فيستدلون به على كمال قدرته وفضله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r6.claim: The sūra has two denials, of the Qur’an and resurrection; God answers them with paired rejecting questions and distinct endings, making four interrogative forms.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r6.anchor: أتبعه استفهامين إنكاريين منشورين على القولين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r14.claim: The question rebukes those who deny resurrection by pointing to God’s sending water to revive barren land.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r15.claim: God sends the water from either the sky or the earth.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r16.claim: Al-jarz is land whose growth has been cut away by drying and crushing, leaving a smooth surface without vegetation.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r16.anchor: أي التي جزر نباتها أي قطع باليبس والتهشم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-jarz is land where rain falls but is too scant to benefit it; Biqāʿī cites al-Bukhārī for the report.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r17.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إنها التي لا تمطر إلا مطرا لا يغني عنها شيئا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r18.claim: Water draws plants from the earth’s depths by mixing with the soil; their emergence is real, not an illusion like a magician’s trick.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r18.anchor: أي نبتا لا ساق له باختلاط الماء بالتراب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r19.claim: What livestock eat includes the crop’s grain, leaves, straw, and grasses; livestock come first because they sustain people’s livelihoods and bodies, and the passage concerns vegetation generally.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r19.anchor: أي من حبه وورقه وتبنه وحشيشه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r20.claim: Unlike ʿAbasa, this passage names livestock first because it treats vegetation generally; ʿAbasa follows food through to the human meal and lists foods unsuitable for livestock.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r20.anchor: فإن السياق لطعام الإنسان الذي هو نهاية الزرع

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r21.claim: People eat the crop’s grain and its root when it is still green fodder.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r21.anchor: من حبه , وأصله إذا كان بقلا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r22.claim: The visible revival of barren land plainly proves resurrection; one who sees its evidence and persists in denial lacks sight and insight.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p63/r22.anchor: على ما فيها من الدلالة وأصر على الإنكار لا بصر له ولا بصيرة

DURR-FULL:v6p557/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p557/r1.speaker: الربيع بن سيرة
DURR-FULL:v6p557/r1.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Sirah says parables bring meanings closer to the mind, citing the example of water driven to barren land and the question ‘do they not see?’
DURR-FULL:v6p557/r1.anchor: عن الربيع بن سيرة قال: الأمثال أقرب إلى العقول من المعاني

BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r7.claim: Driving the water refers to driving water-bearing clouds, which is attributed to God; watering by rivers is attributed to people, though God causes the growth.
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r7.anchor: والمراد سوق السحاب الحامل للماء لأنه هو الذي ينسب إلى الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r8.claim: Al-Baḥr al-ʿulūm takes seeing as knowing, but the author prefers literal sight because the process is perceptible and the verse ends by asking whether they see.
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r8.anchor: حملا على المقصود من النظر أي : قد علموا أنا نسوق الماء

BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r9.claim: Al-jurz is land whose vegetation has been entirely cut away by lack of rain or grazing, not inherently infertile land, since crops then emerge from it.
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r9.anchor: لعدم المطر أو لغيره كالرعي لا التي لا تنبت

BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r10.claim: By the water God brings out crops; zarʿ is originally a verbal noun used for the thing planted.
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r10.anchor: وهو في الأصل مصدر عبر به عن المزروع

BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r11.claim: Livestock eat fodder, straw, leaves, and some grains; people eat food grains and fruit from the crop.
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r11.anchor: كالتبن والقصيل والورق وبعض الحبوب المخصوصة بها

BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r12.claim: The visible provision should lead them to recognize God’s oneness, power, and favor, worship Him alone, and reject even angelic or human partners, let alone lifeless things.
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r12.anchor: فيستدلون به على وحدته وكمال قدرته وفضله تعالى وأنه الحقيق بالعبادة وأن لا يشرك به بعض خلقه من ملك وإنسان فضلا عن جماد

BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r13.claim: The revival of barren land also demonstrates God’s power to restore people to life.
BURSEVI:v7p96#2/r13.anchor: وأيضا فيعلمون أنا نقدر على إعادتهم وإحيائهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r9.claim: Reviving dead land with water and vegetation is evidence of God’s power and the resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r9.anchor: ثم أقام عز وجل الحجة عليهم في معنى الإيمان بالقدرة وبالبعث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r10.claim: The water is driven by clouds; even when it flows in a river, its origin is the clouds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r10.anchor: و «السوق» هو بالسحاب، وإن كان سوق بنهر فأصله من السحاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r11.claim: Al-jurz is land parched until thirst has consumed its vegetation; the word also describes a voracious eater, as in the poet’s line.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r11.anchor: والجرز الأرض العاطشة التي قد أكلت نباتها من العطش والغيظ،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r12.claim: Calling al-jurz simply land that produces nothing is imprecise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p365#2/r12.anchor: ومن عبر عنها بأنها الأرض التي لا تنبت فإنها عبارة غير مخلصة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r1.claim: The verse covers every land having this parched quality, since the sign and lesson are evident in all such places.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r1.anchor: الصفة لأن الآية فيها والعبرة بينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others identify al-jurz as land in Abyan, Yemen, watered by flood streams rather than rain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وغيره الأرض الجرز أرض أبين من اليمن، وهي أرض تشرب بسيول لا بمطر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r3.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r3.claim: The majority pronounce the rāʾ with ḍamma; al-Zajjāj also reports a reading with the rāʾ quiescent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r3.anchor: وجمهور الناس على ضم الراء، وقال الزجاج وتقرأ «الجرز» بسكون الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r4.claim: “Crops” are singled out as an honored, principal product but stand broadly for vegetation here, since livestock usually eat other plants; animals and humans are then named as consumers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r4.anchor: ثم خص تعالى «الزرع» بالذكر تشريفا ولأنه عظم ما يقصد من النبات،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r5.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش وأبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r5.claim: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh and Abū Ḥaywa read yaʾkulu with a masculine yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر بن عياش وأبو حيوة «يأكل» بالياء من تحت،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وجمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads yubṣirūn with yāʾ; the majority read tubṣirūn with tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p366/r6.anchor: ابن مسعود «يبصرون» ، وقرأ جمهور الناس «تبصرون» بالتاء من فوق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r1.claim: The water is rain and flood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r1.anchor: أو لم يروا أنا نسوق الماء يعني المطر والسيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r2.claim: Al-juruz is land that does not grow vegetation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r2.anchor: إلى الأرض الجرز وهي التي لا تنبت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r3.claim: When water reaches the barren land, it produces crops that people and livestock eat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p344#4/r3.anchor: فاذا جاء الماء أنبت فيها ما يأكل الناس والأنعام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r2.claim: God shows kindness by conveying water to people when needed, either from the sky or through running water carried by rivers and descending from mountains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r2.anchor: يبين تعالى لطفه بخلقه، وإحسانه إليهم في إرساله الماء إما من السماء أو من السيح، وهو: ما تحمله الأنهار وينحدر من الجبال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r3.claim: Al-ard al-jurz is land with no vegetation, as in the verse about making the earth a barren plain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r3.anchor: وهي [الأرض] (4) التي لا نبات فيها، كما قال تعالى: {وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا} [الكهف: 8]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r4.claim: The phrase does not mean Egypt alone, though Egypt is certainly included: its soft, heavy, saline, sandy soil needs the Nile’s rain-fed overflow and red silt, which allows crops to grow each year.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r4.anchor: وليس المراد من قوله: {إلى الأرض الجرز} أرض مصر فقط، بل هي بعض المقصود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r5.speaker: قيس بن حجاج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r5.claim: An account transmitted through Ibn Lahīʿa and Qays ibn Hajjaj says that after Egypt’s conquest, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs stopped the annual drowning of a dressed virgin in the Nile; ʿUmar sent a letter invoking God, after which the river rose sixteen cubits overnight and the custom ended.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p372#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن لهيعة، عن قيس بن حجاج، عمن حدثه قال: لما فتحت مصر، أتى أهلها عمرو بن العاص -[وكان أميرا بها] (2) -حين دخل بؤونة من أشهر العجم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r1.claim: The image of water producing crops is linked to the passage describing rain poured down, earth split, and crops and food grown for people and livestock.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r1.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه. أنا صببنا الماء صبا. ثم شققنا الأرض شقا. فأنبتنا فيها حبا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says al-ard al-jurz is land where rain is too slight to help, so it depends on floods.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r2.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن رجل، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إلى الأرض الجرز} قال: هي التي لا تمطر إلا مطرا لا يغني عنها شيئا، إلا ما يأتيها من السيول.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid identify al-ard al-jurz as land in Yemen.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس، ومجاهد: هي أرض باليمن.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r4.claim: Al-Hasan identifies al-ard al-jurz as villages between Yemen and Syria.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن، رحمه الله: هي قرى فيما بين اليمن والشام.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r5.speaker: عكرمة، والضحاك، وقتادة، والسدي، وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r5.claim: ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak, Qatada, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd define al-ard al-jurz as dusty land without vegetation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r5.anchor: الأرض الجرز: التي لا نبات فيها وهي مغبرة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir favors the general sense of dead, barren land brought back to life and producing food, linking it to the sign of the revived earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p373/r6.anchor: قلت: وهذا كقوله: {وآية لهم الأرض الميتة أحييناها

JISHUMI:v8p5688/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5688/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5688/r6.claim: Suq means urging something onward in its movement.

JISHUMI:v8p5688/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5688/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5688/r7.claim: Al-jarz is dry, plantless land after rain has ceased; the term is associated with cutting, exhaustive grazing, gluttony, and land stripped of vegetation, and has three vowelled forms.
JISHUMI:v8p5688/r7.anchor: والجرز: الأرض اليابسة لا نبات بها لانقطاع الأمطار عنها، وأصله من قولهم: سيف جراز، أي: قطع لا يبقي شيئا

JISHUMI:v8p5688/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5688/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5688/r8.claim: The gloss also calls a camel that eats everything and a voracious man jarāz/jarūz, and says the land is “stripped” when its plants are eaten.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r1.claim: The water is driven either as rain and snow or through rivers and springs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r1.anchor: أحدهما : بالمطر والثلج . الثاني : بالأنهار والعيون

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r2.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam defines al-arḍ al-juruz as dry land.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r2.anchor: أحدها : أنها الأرض اليابسة , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r3.claim: Ibn Shajara defines it as land whose crops and trees have been consumed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r3.anchor: الثاني : أنها الأرض التي أكلت ما فيها من زرع وشجر ، قاله ابن شجرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is land reached by water only when floods run to it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r4.anchor: الثالث : أنها الأرض التي لا يأتيها الماء إلا من السيول ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies it as Abyan, a land that does not grow crops.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r5.anchor: الرابع : أنها أرض أبين لا تنبت ، قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r6.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r6.claim: Al-Hasan identifies it as villages of Nabiya between Yemen and Syria.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r6.anchor: الخامس : أنها قرى نبيا بين اليمن والشام ، قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r7.claim: The root denotes cutting: a jarāz sword cuts, a jarāz she-camel eats everything without leaving anything, and a voracious man is called jarūz.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r7.anchor: وأصل الجرز الانقطاع مأخوذ من قولهم سيف جراز أي قطاع وناقة جراز

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r8.claim: A rajaz line calls a man a voracious eater who eats dates without discarding their pits, illustrating jarūz.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r8.anchor: قال الراجز : حب جروز وإذا جاع بكى … يأكل التمر ولا يلقى النوى

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ reads the verse inwardly as the blessings of admonition reaching hardened hearts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p367/r9.anchor: وتأول ابن عطاء هذه الآية على أنه توصل بركات المواعظ إلى القلوب القاسية

MUJAHID:v2p511#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p511#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p511#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the barren land as receiving only ineffective rain, apart from what reaches it in torrents.
MUJAHID:v2p511#2/r1.anchor: عن من حدثه عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ الأرض الجرز ﴾ يعني الأرض التي لا تمطر إلا مطرا لا يغني عنها شيئا إلا ما يأتيها من السيول

MUQATIL:32:27-29/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:32:27-29/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:32:27-29/r1.claim: Al-jarz is smooth land with no vegetation.
MUQATIL:32:27-29/r1.anchor: الأرض الجرز } يعنى الملساء ليس فيها نبت

MUQATIL:32:27-29/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:32:27-29/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:32:27-29/r2.claim: God brings forth crops from the water for their livestock and themselves; these marvels should lead them to affirm God's oneness.
MUQATIL:32:27-29/r2.anchor: فنخرج به } بالماء { زرعا تأكل منه أنعامهم وأنفسهم أفلا يبصرون } [آية: 27] هذه الأعاجيب فيوحدون ربهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r1.claim: God sends rain and rivers toward the barren land.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r2.claim: Al-jarz is land whose plants were cut by drought or grazing, not inherently infertile salt flats, since plants grow there.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r2.anchor: أى الأرض التى جرز نباتها أى قطع اما لعدم الماء أو لانه رعى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r3.claim: Water brings crops whose stalks feed livestock and grain feeds people.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r3.anchor: بالماء ﴿ زرعا تأكل منه ﴾ من الزرع ﴿ أنعامهم ﴾ من عصفه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r4.claim: Seeing the revived land should lead people to infer God's power to resurrect the dead.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p293#5/r4.anchor: بأعينهم فيستدلوا به على قدرته على احياء الموتى

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r1.claim: The verse asks whether people recognize God's complete power in bringing water to lifeless, dry land and reviving it with crops.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r1.anchor: أي أولم يعلموا كمال قدرتنا بسوقنا الماء إلى الأرض اليابسة

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari defines jarz land as land whose plants were cut away for lack of water or through grazing; salty flats are not called jarz.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r2.anchor: الزمخشري: الجرز الأرض التي جرز نباتها، أي قطع

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the jarz land as a region in Yemen.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r5.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r5.claim: Ikrima explains it as thirsty land.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r6.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak calls it dead, thirsty land.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هي الأرض الميتة العطشى

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ defines it as land with no vegetation.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: هي الأرض التي لا نبات فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r8.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r8.claim: Al-Asmaʿi defines it as land that grows nothing at all.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r8.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: هي الأرض التي لا تنبت شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r9.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid doubts that the word denotes a specific region because it has the definite article, though he allows such naming on the model of al-Abbas and al-Dahhak.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r9.anchor: وقال محمد بن يزيد: يبعد أن تكون لأرض بعينها

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r10.claim: The author favors allowing the Yemen identification: the Ibn Abbas transmission is sound, and jarz can be a descriptive adjective with the definite article.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r10.anchor: والإسناد عن ابن عباس صحيح لا مطعن فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r11.claim: The adjective derives from a man called jarūz, who leaves nothing uneaten; the cited rajaz line uses jarūz for such a voracious person.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r11.anchor: رجل جروز إذا كان لا يبقي شيئا إلا أكله

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r12.speaker: الفراء وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r12.claim: Al-Farraʾ and others report four vocalized forms for the word for jarz land, as with bukhl, raghb, and rahb.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r12.anchor: وحكى الفراء وغيره أنه يقال: أرض جرز وجرز

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r13.claim: A report says the land has no rivers and lies far from the sea; it receives a yearly Wadān, allowing three plantings yearly.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r13.anchor: وقد روي أن هذه الأرض لا أنهار فيها، وهي بعيدة

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r14.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r14.claim: Mujahid also identifies the land as the land of the Nile.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r14.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا: أنها أرض النيل

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r15.claim: The pronoun in ‘by it’ refers to the water.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r16.claim: Their livestock eat grasses and herbage from the crops, while people eat grains, greens, and fruits.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r16.anchor: تأكل منه أنعامهم } من الكلأ والحشيش

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r17.claim: Seeing this revival should teach them that God has power to resurrect them.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r17.anchor: يبصرون } هذا فيعلمون أنا نقدر على إعادتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r18.claim: Fanukh'rij may coordinate with nasūq, or it may begin a new clause disconnected from what precedes.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r18.anchor: يكون معطوفا على «نسوق» أو منقطعا مما قبله

QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:27/r19.claim: The clause taʾkulu minhu is in the accusative as an adjective describing the crop.

STUDYQURAN:32:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:27/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:27/r1.claim: They most likely refers to disbelievers among the Quraysh.
STUDYQURAN:32:27/r1.anchor: They is most likely a reference to disbelievers among the Quraysh

STUDYQURAN:32:27/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:27/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:27/r2.claim: The revival of barren earth shows that the disbelievers fail to thank God for provision and to understand how He can resurrect the dead.
STUDYQURAN:32:27/r2.anchor: they fail both to be thankful for the manner in which He provides for them

STUDYQURAN:32:27/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:27/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:27/r3.claim: The dead land can also signify the dead heart, making revival of earth an image of spiritual revivification.
STUDYQURAN:32:27/r3.anchor: the dead land serving as a metonym for the dead heart

TAB-FULL:v18p641/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r1.claim: The earth is dry, hard, and barren; God sends water to it and brings out crops eaten by livestock and people as a sign to those denying resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r1.anchor: نسوق الماء إلى الأرض اليابسة الغليظة التي لا نبات فيها

TAB-FULL:v18p641/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r2.claim: The root evokes a camel that consumes everything; al-arḍ al-jurūz leaves nothing on its surface, and the same term describes a glutton and a sword that cuts all it meets.
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r2.anchor: ناقة جرز: إذا كانت تأكل كل شيء، وكذلك الأرض الجروز: التي لا يبقى على ظهرها شيء إلا أفسدته نظير أكل الناقة الجراز

TAB-FULL:v18p641/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r3.speaker: الراجز
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r3.claim: An unnamed rajaz poet uses jurūz for a voracious eater, illustrating the word's association with consuming everything.
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r3.anchor: كما قال الراجز: [البحر الرجز] خب جروز وإذا

TAB-FULL:v18p641/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī lists four dialectal vocalizations for the word and reports that the fatḥ form belongs to Banū Tamīm.
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r4.anchor: فيه لغات أربع: أرض جرز، وجرز، وجرز وجرز، والفتح لبني تميم فيما بلغني

TAB-FULL:v18p641/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the barren land as a place in Yemen.
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: «الأرض الجرز، أرض باليمن»

TAB-FULL:v18p641/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r6.claim: Mujāhid identifies it as Abyan and similar lands.
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء، إلى الأرض الجرز}

TAB-FULL:v18p641/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r7.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās describes the land as receiving only ineffective rain, except for water arriving through floods.
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r7.anchor: عن رجل، عن ابن عباس، في قوله " {إلى الأرض الجرز}

TAB-FULL:v18p641/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the land as having no vegetation.

TAB-FULL:v18p641/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r9.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r9.claim: Qatāda describes the land as dusty.
TAB-FULL:v18p641/r9.anchor: عن قتادة، " {أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء، إلى الأرض الجرز}

TAB-FULL:v18p643/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p643/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p643/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says al-arḍ al-juruz is land with nothing on it and no vegetation.
TAB-FULL:v18p643/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز}

TAB-FULL:v18p643/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p643/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p643/r2.claim: The commentary links this phrase with 18:8, where Ibn Zayd says ṣaʿīdan juruz is land with nothing on it and no vegetation.

SULAMI:v2p139#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p139#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p139#3/r1.claim: God brings the blessings of admonitions to hard hearts that turn away from the Real, so they may take heed.
SULAMI:v2p139#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : نوصل بركات المواعظ إلى القلوب القاسية

TABATABAI:32:25-29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r5.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses driving as urging something onward and barren land as dry ground without plants because rains have ceased; zarʿ is a verbal noun used here for crops.
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r5.anchor: قال في المجمع السوق الحث على السير من ساقه يسوقه

TABATABAI:32:25-29/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r6.claim: Rain-bearing clouds are driven to barren land; rain revives it into crops that feed people and livestock, displaying God's wise care especially for living beings.
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r6.anchor: والمراد بسوق الماء إلى الأرض الخالية من النبات

TABATABAI:32:25-29/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r7.claim: The closing question warns and reproaches; sight is specified because rain, crops, and their use by humans and livestock are directly seen.
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r7.anchor: تنبيه وتوبيخ وتخصيص هذه الآية بالإبصار

TABATABAI:32:25-29/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r8.claim: The former nations are known through reports heard, while rain reviving barren land and feeding animals and people is known by sight.
TABATABAI:32:25-29/r8.anchor: والآية السابقة بالسمع لما أن العلم بإهلاك الأمم الماضين إنما هو بالأخبار التي تنال من طريق السمع

TABRISI:32:26-28/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:26-28/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:26-28/r6.claim: Sūq means urging or driving along; sāqahu yasūquhu means he drove it.
TABRISI:32:26-28/r6.anchor: والسوق الحث على السير ساقه يسوقه

TABRISI:32:26-28/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:26-28/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:26-28/r7.claim: Al-jurz is dry, plantless land after rain ceases; its root is linked to cutting and to a voracious eater. Four vowel patterns are listed, with a rajaz verse illustrating jarūz.
TABRISI:32:26-28/r7.anchor: الجزر الأرض اليابسة التي ليس فيها نبات لانقطاع الأمطار عنها

TABRISI:32:26-28/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:26-28/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:26-28/r8.claim: The subject of yahdi is implicit, supplied by “how many We destroyed”; kam is the object of ahlaknā, and yamshūn is circumstantial.
TABRISI:32:26-28/r8.anchor: فاعل يهد مضمر يدل عليه قوله

TABRISI:32:26-28/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:26-28/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:26-28/r12.claim: God drives water to sterile land through rain and snow; another view says through rivers and springs.

TABRISI:32:26-28/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:26-28/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:32:26-28/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says torrents carry water to dry high places in settlements between Syria and Yemen.

TABRISI:32:26-28/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:26-28/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:26-28/r14.claim: Water produces crops for livestock and people, displaying God’s favors.
TABRISI:32:26-28/r14.anchor: والمعنى أن هذه الأرض تنبت ما يأكله الناس والأنعام

FARRA:v2p333/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p333/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p333/r3.claim: الجرز is land without vegetation; related forms describe a camel or person that eats everything and a sword that cuts everything. Multiple vocalizations of أرض جرز are acceptable, like the four forms of البخل and related words.
FARRA:v2p333/r3.anchor: وقوله: إلى الأرض الجرز [27] والجرز: التي لا نبات فيها: ويقال للناقة: إنها لجراز إذا كانت تأكل كل شيء

THALABI:v7p334#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p334#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p334#2/r1.claim: Jurz describes land stripped bare: the root can describe locusts consuming a crop completely, and a cutting sword; the word has four dialectal forms.
THALABI:v7p334#2/r1.anchor: وسيف جراز أي قاطع، وجرزت الجراد الزرع إذا استأصلته، فكأن الجرز هي الأرض التي لا يبقى على ظهرها شيء إلا أفسدته، وفيه أربع لغات:

THALABI:v7p334#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p334#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p334#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the barren land as a land in Yemen.
THALABI:v7p334#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي أرض باليمن. قال مجاهد:

THALABI:v7p334#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p334#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p334#2/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the barren land as Abyan.
THALABI:v7p334#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: هي أبين فنخرج فننبت به زرعا تأكل منه أنعامهم وأنفسهم أفلا يبصرون.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p347/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p347/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p347/r1.claim: Al-jarz is hard, dry land without vegetation; its plural is ajrāz, and drought years are called sunūn ajrāz.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p347/r1.anchor: الأرض الجرز} الغليظة اليابسة التي لا نبت فيها (1) . وجمعها:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r1.claim: Muqātil says this is an admonition urging them to be wary.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the water brought to the land as a torrent.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj define al-jurz as land that does not grow vegetation; the word has four dialectal vocalizations, like al-shughl and al-bukhl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r3.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج: هي التي لا تنبت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r4.claim: The commentary has already discussed the meaning and derivation of al-jurz under the Cave sūra’s verse 8.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r4.anchor: وذكرنا تفسير الجرز واشتقاقه في سورة الكهف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies a particular land in Yemen without seas or rivers; unexpected torrents reach it, allowing people to sow whatever grain they wish.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أرضا باليمن ليس فيها بحار ولا أنهار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r6.claim: Mujāhid describes land that grows only when it receives floodwater rather than rain.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda locates al-jurz in the region of Aden, treating it as a particular place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r7.anchor: وهذا قول أبي عبيدة قال: إنها بناحية عدن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r8.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad says that if al-jurz is a place-name for a particular land, the definite article is linguistically unexpected for a proper name; it is possible for names originally used as shared descriptions, like al-Madīna and al-Baṣra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r8.anchor: قال المبرد (¬2): على هذا القول إنها أرض بعينها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r9.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r9.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains the article in transferred descriptive names as retaining a notional trace of the description when it becomes a proper name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r9.anchor: وسبب دخول اللام على هذه الأسماء مع كونها معارف أنها أوصاف نقلت فصارت أعلاما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r10.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r10.claim: Al-Suddī says it is dead land without vegetation until water arrives and produces plants eaten by people and animals; Muqātil gives a similar explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r10.anchor: وقال السدي في هذه الآية: هي الأرض الميتة التي لا نبات لها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r11.claim: Al-Suddī’s general reading is better because it matches the nearby argument against deniers of resurrection: God revives dead land; the passage names no particular place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r11.anchor: وهذا القول كان أجود؛ لأنه أشبه بنظائر هذه الآية من الاحتجاج على منكري البعث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r12.claim: On the general reading of dead land, the water may be rain or a torrent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p161/r12.anchor: وعلى هذا القول قوله: {الماء إلى الأرض الجرز} يجوز أن يكون المطر ويجوز أن يكون يريد السيل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:27/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:27/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:27/r1.claim: The barren land is hard, with no vegetation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:27/r1.anchor: الغليظة التي لا نبات فيها { فنخرج به زرعا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:27/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:27/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:27/r2.claim: Sending water that produces crops for people and livestock is evidence that God can resurrect the dead.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:27/r2.anchor: هذا فيعلموا أنا نقدر على إعادتهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r2.claim: The people asked whether they see are the polytheists.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r3.claim: The water is rain, carried in clouds that are driven along.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r3.anchor: يعني: المطر، تساق السحاب التي فيها الماء. كقوله

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r4.claim: The barren land is dry and has no plants.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r4.anchor: {إلى الأرض الجرز} [السجدة: 27] اليابسة التي ليس فيها نبات.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r5.claim: The wording recalls 7:57, where God says He drives rain to a dead land.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r6.claim: The question about seeing is directed to the polytheists.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r6.anchor: يعني: المشركين. أي فالذي أحيا هذه الأرض بعد موتها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r7.claim: The One who revives the earth after its death is able to resurrect people after their death.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p695/r7.anchor: أي فالذي أحيا هذه الأرض بعد موتها قادر على أن يحييهم بعد موتهم.

MAJAZ:v2p133/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p133/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p133/r3.claim: Al-jarz is hard, dry land that has received no rain.
MAJAZ:v2p133/r3.anchor: أي الغليظة اليابسة التي لم يصبها مطر

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:25/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:25/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:25/r1.claim: The sūra opens by asking deniers to reflect on creation and its directing power, and closes by warning that persistent rejection leads to an unavoidable painful end and that the Prophet cannot do more than convey the message.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:25/r1.anchor: Allah katından gelen bildirimleri düzmece olarak niteleyen inkârcılara evrendeki olaylar ve bunlara yön veren yüce kudret üzerinde düşünme çağrısı yaparak başlayan sûre, buna paralel bir içerikle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:25/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:25/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:25/r2.claim: To help people recognize their helplessness before God's power and the truth of His promise, verses 26 and 27 invite reflection using archaeology and empirical sciences such as geophysics and agriculture.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:25/r2.anchor: İnsanlar, Allah’ın kudreti karşısında kendilerinin ne kadar âciz olduğunu ve O’nun vaadinin gerçekliğini anlamaları için 26. âyette arkeoloji gibi beşerî bilimlerin, 27. âyette de jeofizik ve ziraat gibi deneysel bilimlerin verileri ışığında düşünmeye davet edilmekte

BURHAN:v3p375/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p375/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p375/r1.claim: Raising فنخرج establishes the greening; making it subjunctive would reverse the point and imply failure to give thanks, as Zamakhshari explains.
BURHAN:v3p375/r1.anchor: الرابع أنه لو نصب لأعطى ما هو عكس الغرض لأن معناه إثبات الاخضرار

BURHAN:v3p375/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p375/r2.speaker: ابن الخباز
BURHAN:v3p375/r2.claim: Ibn al-Khabaz says the subjunctive would spoil the meaning: seeing the water is not what causes greening; the water itself does.
BURHAN:v3p375/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الخباز النصب يفسد المعنى لأن رؤية المخاطب الماء الذي أنزله الله ليس سببا للاخضرار

BURHAN:v3p375/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p375/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p375/r3.claim: The present verb فتثير among past verbs makes the wind's cloud-raising vivid and certain to the listener.
BURHAN:v3p375/r3.anchor: ﴿ والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلى بلد ميت ﴾

BURHAN:v3p375/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p375/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p375/r4.claim: Although reviving earth matters, stirring clouds is more astonishing because its cause is hidden; people recognize water's effect on crops more readily than wind's role in rain.
BURHAN:v3p375/r4.anchor: وإثارة السحاب أعجبها فكان أولى بالتخصيص بالمضارع وإنما قال إن إثارة السحاب أعجب

NAHHAS:v3p298/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p298/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the barren land as Yemen; al-Nahhas says the report's chain is sound and unassailable.
NAHHAS:v3p298/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال هي أرض اليمن

NAHHAS:v3p298/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r10.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v3p298/r10.claim: Mujahid identifies the land as Abyan.
NAHHAS:v3p298/r10.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال هي أبين

NAHHAS:v3p298/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r11.speaker: عكرمة
NAHHAS:v3p298/r11.claim: Ikrima describes the land as thirsty; al-Dahhak calls it dead and thirsty.
NAHHAS:v3p298/r11.anchor: عن عكرمة إلى الأرض الجرز قال هي الظمأى وقال جويبر عن الضحاك

NAHHAS:v3p298/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r12.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p298/r12.claim: Al-Farra and al-Asma'i define الجرز as land that grows nothing.
NAHHAS:v3p298/r12.anchor: قال الفراء هي التي لا نبات فيها وقال الأصمعي الأرض الجرز التي لا تنبت شيئا

NAHHAS:v3p298/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r13.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v3p298/r13.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid says the definite article suggests a particular land, though a generic reading is possible under reported views.
NAHHAS:v3p298/r13.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد يبعد أن تكون إلا أرضا بعينها لدخول الألف واللام

NAHHAS:v3p298/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p298/r14.claim: Al-Nahhas answers that الجرز is an adjective and may take the definite article; it derives from a voracious eater that leaves nothing.
NAHHAS:v3p298/r14.anchor: وهذا إنما هو نعت والنعت للمعرفة يكون بالألف واللام وهو مشتق من قولهم رجل جروز

NAHHAS:v3p298/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p298/r15.claim: The source records jarz, jaraz, and jurz as dialect forms, like variants of بخْل and رعب.
NAHHAS:v3p298/r15.anchor: وحكى الفراء وغيره أنه يقال أرض جرز وجرز وجرز وكذلك بخل ورعب ورهب

NAHHAS:v3p298/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p298/r16.claim: فنخرج may coordinate with نسوق or start a clause disconnected from what precedes.
NAHHAS:v3p298/r16.anchor: يكون معطوفا على نسوق أو منقطعا مما قبله

NAHHAS:v3p298/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p298/r17.claim: تأكل منه أنعامهم is an accusative adjective qualifying زرعا.

NAHHAS:v3p298/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p298/r18.claim: وأنفسهم means the people also eat from the crop, with the verb understood.

NAHHAS:v3p298/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p298/r19.claim: Arabic uses نفس for an individual distinct from others and for a thing's whole self or reality; the verse on God's knowledge illustrates the latter.
NAHHAS:v3p298/r19.anchor: والنفس في كلام العرب على ضربين أحدهما أنه يراد بها الانفصال والآخر أنه يراد بها جملة الشيء وحقيقته

NAHHAS:v3p298/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p298/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p298/r20.claim: ألا here serves as an alerting particle.

BURHAN:v1p79/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p79/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p79/r1.claim: The endings match the kind of evidence: the account of destroyed generations is heard, while the water and crops are seen.
BURHAN:v1p79/r1.anchor: لأن سوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز مرئى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/f14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/f14.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#3/f14.claim: After crops, livestock precede people in 32:27; the human-food passage in 80:31–32 lists human nourishment before animal fodder.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r11.claim: The water being driven to barren land and producing crops is visible, so the verse appropriately uses both seeing and looking language.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r11.anchor: لأن سوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز مرئي
